# Disagreement Log — T12_009 (Testament of Gad)
**Chapter:** T12_009 | **Verses:** 7 sections (~9 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 1:4 | Hatred metaphor | "devour-him-out-of-my-life, as-a-bull-devours-the-grass" | Same | "wanted to erase him from the earth the way a bull tears through a field" | EMET/LOGOS literal retained — the bull-grass image is precise and striking |
| 2 | 3:3 | Hatred's social behavior | Full clause "urgent that he should be judged...punished...put to death" | Same | Summarized as "wants judgment and punishment and death" | EMET/LOGOS sequence preserved — the three-stage escalation matters |
| 3 | 5:4 | Forgiveness formula | "seventy-times-in-a-day" | "seven times in a day" | "seventy times in a day" | "seventy times in a day" — EMET/PNEUMA; the Greek MS has hebdomēkontakis (seventy times), echoing Mt 18:22 |
| 4 | 4:1 | Love/hatred antithesis | "love-would-quicken-even-the-dead...hatred-would-slay-the-living" | Same | "love can call back the dead; hatred will kill the living" | All three agree on substance; SOPHIA adopts formal phrasing |
| 5 | 5:5 | "Leave to God the avenging" | Present | Present (variant: "leave the avenging") | "leave the settling of accounts to God" | "leave to God the avenging" — EMET/LOGOS phrasing; "avenging" is Greek ekdikēsis |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Gad is the direct counterpart to Testament of Zebulun — where Zebulun chose compassion after Joseph's suffering, Gad chose hatred, and this chapter is his repentance. The "seventy times" forgiveness formula (5:4) is theologically significant and anticipates the Synoptic tradition. The hatred catalogue (4:3) is one of the most sustained rhetorical passages in the Testaments.*
